cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Put It Back Quietly
cards.instruction: Return something you misplaced, used, or damaged without revealing why it needed restoring.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's handle this professionally. I've put your umbrella back in the stand. You'll want it for work.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why is it wet? It hasn't rained.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I can explain the standard again. Slowly. I gave it a rinse. I'll dry the handle before you go.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's pondweed caught in the spokes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then it needs another rinse. Have breakfast; I'll get it back in the stand properly this time.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 and A3 professional wrappers add no precise restoration technique, while the rinse explanations conceal the prior use.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 wet-without-rain causes A3 rinse cover; B4 pondweed causes A5 another rinse and return promise.

relationship.evidence: B2 and B4 question the condition of B own umbrella and supply incriminating details.

heightening.evidence: A5 treats B4 evidence as more cleaning instead of explaining how it got there.

specificity.evidence: A1 returned umbrella for work and B4 pondweed make hidden misuse legible.

brevityWit.evidence: A3 standard-again-slowly interrupts a simple cover story without a useful correction.
